old: Strong electrolytes: $\Lambda_m$ rises slowly and linearly with $\sqrt{c}$ (Debye-Huckel-Onsager)
new: Strong electrolytes: $\Lambda_m$ increases slowly on dilution and decreases linearly with $\sqrt{c}$ ($\Lambda_m = \Lambda_m^\circ - A\sqrt{c}$)
fixes: Direction of Λm vs √c for strong electrolytes

old: $\Delta G$ in J = n x F x E with E in volts
new: $\Delta G$ (in J) = $-nFE$, with F in C mol$^{-1}$ and E in volts
$E_{cell} > 0$, $\Delta G < 0$: spontaneous under the given conditions; separately, $E^\circ_{cell} > 0$, $\Delta G^\circ < 0$: $K > 1$
fixes: K > 1 follows from E°cell > 0 (ΔG° < 0), not from E_cell > 0

old: Alkali metals are always $+1$ and alkaline earth metals are always $+2$
new: In their compounds, alkali metals are always $+1$ and alkaline earth metals are always $+2$
fixes: Alkali/alkaline earth ON rule applies only to compounds (free state is 0)
